metadata.title: Machine-checked involution theorems in Lean 4 — 95 theorems, axiom accounting, 3 candidate originals
metadata.description:
A machine-checked corpus of 95 theorems in Lean 4, across 12 files, compiling with no Mathlib and no sorry.

This deposit proves no Clay Millennium Prize Problem. It proves the involution each problem is stated across, machine-checked, and an involution is not the conjecture.

What is actually established. Of the 95 theorems, machine verification reports that the great majority depend on NO axiom at all — they are decided by computation in the kernel, so the proof is the computation and nothing is assumed — and the remainder depend on propext alone, which is one of Lean’s three foundational axioms and is what its own core arithmetic reasons through. None depends on Classical.choice, and none on sorryAx. That accounting is re-derived on every run by asking the kernel with #print axioms, never by restating it.

Priority is claimed over 3 results, each with a prior-art search on record that returned nothing:

  • Closure is one hundred sixty two (three.lean)
  • The closure is eighty one orbits (three.lean)
  • Reflection complements the address (three.lean)

The remaining 92 are FORMALISATIONS of known results and each carries its citation. Nothing here claims to have discovered the pinhole camera, central inversion, or row-major addressing.

A DOI dates an expression; it does not establish novelty. What is claimed above is the expression, dated by this deposit.
metadata.notes: Publish as an INDEPENDENT deposit with its own DOI, relating back to the earlier record — NOT as a new version under the shared concept DOI, which resolves to a different work and whose version chain is shared by three unrelated projects.
